title: Episodic Compression Sprint — notes and mini-experiments
content:
TL;DR:
- Sprint goal: test lightweight episodic compression (lossy but retrieval-preserving) as a on-load mitigation for long-context apps. Tradeoff: token savings vs. downstream generation quality and retrieval latency.
- Early idea: compress 'session events' into compact KV chunks using a combined heuristic (topic-similarity + surprisal delta) then store in KV shard; decompress on-demand using cheap local decoder or retrieve compressed + augment prompt.

Papers / reads (quick takeaways):
- Chen et al. 2025 (Contextual Compression via KV Distillation): distillation into short keys works if you preserve alignment score with original prefix; note: they use teacher perplexity as a compression fidelity metric — seems promising for offline eval.
- Navarro & Li 2026 (Sparse Episodic Memory for LMs): shows sparse indexing + cluster centroid signatures can reduce retrieval cost, but centroid mismatch hurts retrieval for niche queries.
- Workshop talk (NeurIPS 2026): "Compression-aware caching" — main takeaway: cache keys should encode both topical signal and token-level predictive uncertainty.

Personal observations (from skims + small local tests):
- Simple topic-cluster compression (SBERT->kmeans->store centroid) saves ~60% tokens but causes 8-12% drop in answer F1 for targeted QA when cluster is noisy.
- Compressing by 'surprisal threshold' (keep tokens with high surprisal relative to local LM) keeps answer quality but saves less (~20-30%).
- Combined heuristic (topic + surprisal) seems best: aims to keep rare/important tokens that are predictive for downstream tasks.

Hypotheses to test formally:
1) Combined heuristic reduces cost by >=40% while keeping downstream QA BLEU/F1 within 5% of full context baseline on our chat eval.
2) Local cheap decoder (distilled 1B) can approximate decompression with <10ms latency added at inference for 512-token compressed chunk.
3) Compression + delta-retrieval (store compressed chunk + small delta of recent tokens) provides graceful degradation vs pure compression when queries are near-term.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Datasets: customer-chat-sim (internal, 8k sessions), doc-summaries (1k long docs).
- Compression methods: token-surprisal prune, sbt-topic-cluster, kv-distill (teacher-based), combined-heuristic.
- Retrieval modes: exact-key, approximate (HNSW), compressed+delta.
- Metrics: tokens-saved, avg-latency (hosted), QA-F1, generation-ROUGE, model-perp-on-decompressed-prefix, end-to-end cost-per-response.
- SLO targets: p95 latency <= 350ms for <1kB compressed fetch; cost reduction >=30% target for dedicated use-case.

Small prototype pseudocode (sketch):
- compress_session(session_text):
    embeddings = embed(sentences)
    clusters = cluster(embeddings, k=heuristic_k)
    for c in clusters:
      keep_tokens = [t for t in c if surprisal(t) > tau or is_entity(t)]
      key = centroid(embeddings_of(keep_tokens))[:128-dim]
      value = join(keep_tokens)  # lossy, preserves rare tokens
      store_kv(key, compress_bytes(value))

Notes on metrics to instrument (internal):
- Store both token_count_before and token_count_after in Console per-session.
- Tag retrieval results with compression-method and compression-version.
- Emit a fidelity_score = teacher_perp(decompressed_prefix) vs teacher_perp(original_prefix).

Preliminary results from local run (mini dataset, 200 sessions):
- token-surprisal-prune: tokens_saved=28% | QA-F1 drop=4.7% | avg-retrieval-size=430B
- sbt-topic-cluster: tokens_saved=61% | QA-F1 drop=11.9% | avg-retrieval-size=210B
- combined-heuristic: tokens_saved=46% | QA-F1 drop=5.8% | avg-retrieval-size=350B
- Costs: naive compression adds ~12ms per request (encoding+index) during write time; decompression (distilled 1B) measured ~18ms on RTX A10G equivalent.

Open design questions / gotchas:
- Eviction policy: if compressed chunks vary wildly in retrieval utility density, LRU alone may evict important compressed chunks. Need utility-aware eviction score (approx retrieval hit rate * importance).
- Versioning: compressed representation schema will evolve; must add version tags in KV values and graceful fallback to raw event store.
- Security: compressed values may contain PII — ensure compression stage integrates with PII scrubber and KMS tagging.

Quick checklist / TODOs (me and collaborators):
- [ ] Run full 1k-session sweep with combined-heuristic and measure p95 latency on staging dedicated cluster (INF-dedicated-3). (Owner: Sana)
- [ ] Add fidelity metric instrumentation to Console (tag: compression-fidelity). (Owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Prototype local distilled decompressor as a tiny gRPC microservice and measure cold-start overhead. (Owner: Mika)
- [ ] Create Linear ticket to track policy for compressed-evidence retention + export requirement. (linked: INF-4321)

Quick sketches for rollout strategy (ops-friendly):
- Stage 0: Offline-only — produce compressed artifacts, run regressions on eval sets (no changes to live retrieval).
- Stage 1: Read-only retrieval (serve compressed values in parallel but prefer raw when available). Monitor regression windows.
- Stage 2: Canary (5% sessions) small compress+serve; automatic fallback if QA-F1 delta > threshold.
- Stage 3: Gradual ramp with autoscaling on decompressor pool.

Useful links / shorthand references:
- Slack: #research-context-compress (bookmark)
- GH ref impl: github.com/redwood-inference/ctx-compress (branch: episodic-sprint)
- Confluence proto: episodic-compression-proto (linked above)

Open questions for discussion with Eng-Platform:
- What are realistic p95 cold-start targets for small decompressor services on Dedicated? (ask SRE)
- Can we piggyback compressed chunk retrieval onto existing KV shards or is separate index required for approximate retrieval?

Notes-to-self (misc):
- Remember to log small human-readable excerpt of compressed value for auditability.
- For demos, show 'before/after prompt' with visible tokens removed to highlight quality tradeoffs.

Meeting notes (2026-12-03 sync with Ravi & Mika):
- Ravi: want Console charts for tokens saved per-team and per-route; flagged need for cost breakdown by compression compute vs retrieval savings.
- Mika: will try distill-to-decompressor baseline vs on-the-fly reconstruction with model adapter; predicted win for decompressor when compressed chunk > 128 tokens.
- Action: set up staging runs and attach results to Confluence page by EOD 2026-12-17.

End of sprint log for now — rough, messy, intentionally incomplete. Will iterate after staging sweep.

Notes last edited in-line: ask @Ravi for Linear access to INF-4321; add more composed eval prompts for long-tail queries.
